references.text: The original instruction from God to make the courtyard with hangings of fine twisted linen, one hundred cubits long on the south side. Exodus 38:9 describes the execution of this command.
Gives the measurements for the courtyard, including a length of one hundred cubits and hangings of fine twisted linen, matching what was made in Exodus 38:9.
Continues the description of the courtyard's construction, including the pillars, bases, and hooks that go with the hangings mentioned in verse 9.
Mentions the hangings for the courtyard and the tabernacle, showing the continued use of the courtyard structure described in Exodus 38:9.
Solomon's temple also had an inner court, showing continuity in the concept of a holy courtyard from the tabernacle.
Confirms that the material mentioned for the south side applied to the entire courtyard.
The vision in Ezekiel restores the tabernacle's measurements as a symbol of the new order.
The vision's measurements confirm the divine standard set forth in the books of Moses.
